doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Style, originality and the younger generation
title: No resentment of young players being signed
summary: He says he does not resent youngsters' success.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do you feel any, not resentment, but just the irony of something like Columbia seeming to sign every young musician almost on the basis of youth. It seems that you have to be under 25, even if they’re of marginal talent but just the fact that they’re young and can play, I mean it’s not that they’re completely incompetent but they all sound alike, do you sort of resent the attention that’s been focused on this younger movement in jazz?

No, I don’t resent it. I never have been resentment of nobody who’s successful. But I do think they should make an allowance for anybody that’s got the talent whether they’re young or old. ‘Cause I hear some of these youngsters can’t play near as good as some of these old-timers.
